title: The Sunday Read: ‘The Woman Who Could Smell Parkinson’s’

sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: Smell is a powerful sensory capability.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉是一种强大的感官能力。

sentences.en: It's the most evocative sense we have, the one most bound up with memory.
sentences.zh: 这是我们最能唤起回忆的感官，与记忆联系最深。

sentences.en: And we and other animals use it to do some really remarkable stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们和其他动物都用它来做一些非常了不起的事情。

sentences.en: All sorts of species, fish, birds, probably elephants, rely on smell to guide them on their great migrations, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，各种物种，如鱼类、鸟类，可能还有大象，都依靠嗅觉来指引它们的宏大迁徙。

sentences.en: Rats can sniff out landmines.
sentences.zh: 老鼠可以嗅出地雷。

sentences.en: And yet, of our various senses, smell is also the one that we tend to neglect.
sentences.zh: 然而，在我们众多的感官中，嗅觉也是最容易被忽视的一种。

sentences.en: We treat it as if it were a little bit primitive, sort of childish or generally unserious.
sentences.zh: 我们对待它就像对待某种稍微有点原始、有些幼稚或总体上很不严肃的东西一样。

sentences.en: You might say we look down our noses at smell.
sentences.zh: 你可以说我们对嗅觉不屑一顾。

sentences.en: And so, when a woman in Scotland realized that she could actually smell Parkinson's disease, that the illness itself gave off what was, to her, this intense, musty, oily odor,
sentences.zh: 因此，当苏格兰的一名女性意识到自己其实能闻出帕金森病时——这种疾病本身会散发出一种对她而言极其浓烈、霉湿且带有油性的气味——

sentences.en: and gave it off years before a diagnosis, it took a little while before doctors and scientists really began to listen.
sentences.zh: 而且在确诊前几年就能闻出来，医生和科学家们花了相当一段时间才真正开始倾听。

sentences.en: My name is Scott Sayre, and I'm a contributor to the New York Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫斯科特·塞尔（Scott Sayre），是《纽约时报杂志》的撰稿人。

sentences.en: For a recent piece, I spent a bunch of time with Joy Milne, a Scottish retiree with a really extraordinary nose.
sentences.zh: 为了最近的一篇报道，我花了很多时间与乔伊·米尔恩（Joy Milne）相处，她是一位拥有极其非凡嗅觉的苏格兰退休老人。

sentences.en: And you'll hear about her in this week's Sunday Read.
sentences.zh: 在本周的《周日阅读》中，你将听到关于她的故事。

sentences.en: Joy's always been a hyperosmic, or what's maybe better known as a supersmeller.
sentences.zh: 乔伊一直是个超常嗅觉者，或者说得更广为人知一点，是个“超级鼻”。

sentences.en: She actually makes serious adaptations to her life in order to avoid certain scents.
sentences.zh: 为了避开某些气味，她其实对自己的生活做出了重大的调整。

sentences.en: She'll only drink water that comes from a spring, for instance.
sentences.zh: 比如，她只喝泉水。

sentences.en: She changes sidewalks to avoid the stink of men's spray deodorant, which she particularly detests.
sentences.zh: 她会绕路走，以避开男士喷雾除臭剂的恶臭，她尤其讨厌这种味道。

sentences.en: So, one day, many years ago,
sentences.zh: 所以，许多年前的某一天，

sentences.en: Joy caught a whiff of something new on her husband.
sentences.zh: 乔伊在丈夫身上闻到了一股新奇的味道。

sentences.en: A peculiar, unpleasant scent.
sentences.zh: 一种奇怪而令人不快的味道。

sentences.en: Something stale and thick.
sentences.zh: 一种陈腐而厚重的味道。

sentences.en: It was only much later, years after he'd been diagnosed with Parkinson's, that she realized that everyone else she met with Parkinson's smelled exactly the same as he did.
sentences.zh: 直到很久以后，在他被确诊患有帕金森病多年之后，她才意识到，她遇到的其他所有帕金森病患者闻起来都和他一模一样。

sentences.en: When Joy first told scientists about this bizarre realization, not too many of them took her seriously.
sentences.zh: 当乔伊第一次把这个离奇的发现告诉科学家时，并没有多少人把她当回事。

sentences.en: But then they ran some initial tests, and those tests showed that Joy was absolutely, unequivocally capable of telling Parkinson's patients from people without the disease.
sentences.zh: 但后来他们进行了一些初步测试，这些测试表明，乔伊绝对、毫无疑问地能够区分出帕金森病患者和没有这种疾病的人。

sentences.en: They've also now studied her nose quite extensively, and they're using the particulars of what she smells to develop an early diagnostic test for Parkinson's.
sentences.zh: 如今，他们也对她的鼻子进行了相当广泛的研究，并正利用她所闻到的气味特征来开发帕金森病的早期诊断测试。

sentences.en: That's a kind of test that doesn't exist yet for the disease, and one researcher told me it's a kind of holy grail for the field.
sentences.zh: 这种测试对于该病来说目前尚不存在，一位研究人员告诉我，这是该领域梦寐以求的圣杯。

sentences.en: Joy's ability has profoundly shaped her life, as you might imagine, and it might one day shape the lives of many, many other people.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的那样，乔伊的能力深刻地塑造了她的人生，而它有一天可能会塑造许许多多其他人的生活。

sentences.en: But to me, what Joy's really doing is seeing, where until now, medicine has only been able to look.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，乔伊真正做到的，是在医学迄今为止只能进行“观察”的地方进行“感知”。

sentences.en: And she's seeing with her nose.
sentences.zh: 而她是用鼻子去感知的。

sentences.en: So, here's my article,
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我的文章，

sentences.en: The Woman Who Could Smell Parkinson's, read by Robert Petkoff.
sentences.zh: 《能闻出帕金森病的女人》，由罗伯特·佩特科夫（Robert Petkoff）朗读。

sentences.en: Our audio producer today is Adrian HurSt.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的音频制作人是阿德里安·赫斯特（Adrian Hurst）。

sentences.en: The original music you'll hear was written and performed by Aaron Esposito.
sentences.zh: 你将听到的原创音乐由亚伦·埃斯波西托（Aaron Esposito）创作和演奏。

sentences.en: As a boy, Les Milne carried an air of triumph about him, and an air of sorrow.
sentences.zh: 少年时期的莱斯·米尔恩（Les Milne）身上带着一种胜利者的气场，同时也带着一种哀愁。

sentences.en: Les was a particularly promising and energetic young man, an all-Scottish swim champion, head boy at his academy in Dundee, a top student bound for medical school.
sentences.zh: 莱斯是一个特别有前途、充满活力的年轻人，曾是全苏格兰游泳冠军、邓迪学校的学生代表，也是一名准备进入医学院的尖子生。

sentences.en: But when he was young, his father died.
sentences.zh: 但在他年轻时，父亲去世了。

sentences.en: His mother was institutionalized with a diagnosis of manic depression, and he and his younger brother were effectively left to fend for themselves.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲因被诊断患有狂躁抑郁症而被送进精神病院，他和弟弟基本上只能靠自己独立生活。

sentences.en: His high school girlfriend Joy was drawn to him as much by his sadness as his talents, by his yearning for her care.
sentences.zh: 高中女友乔伊被他的悲伤和才华所吸引，也为他渴望得到她照顾的样子所倾倒。

sentences.en: We were very, very much in love,
sentences.zh: “我们曾经非常非常相爱，”

sentences.en: Joy, now a flaxen-haired 72-year-old grandmother, told me recently.
sentences.zh: 如今已是满头金发的72岁祖母乔伊不久前对我说。

sentences.en: In a somewhat less conventional way, she also adored the way Les smelled.
sentences.zh: 以一种略显传统的方式，她同样迷恋莱斯身上的气味。

sentences.en: And this aroma of salt and musk, accented with a suggestion of leather from the carbolic soap he used at the pool, formed for her a lasting sense of who he was.
sentences.zh: 这种混合着盐味和麝香味、并带有他在泳池使用的石炭酸皂所散发出的皮革气息的芳香，在她心中构成了他是谁的持久记忆。

sentences.en: It was just him, Joy said, a steadfast marker of his identity, no less distinctive than his face, his voice, his particular quality of mind.
sentences.zh: 乔伊说，那就是他本人，一个坚定不移的身份标志，其独特性绝不亚于他的面容、他的声音和他的独特心智。

sentences.en: Joy's had always been an unusually sensitive nose, the inheritance she believes of her maternal line.
sentences.zh: 乔伊一直拥有异常敏感的鼻子，她相信这是来自母系家族的遗传。

sentences.en: Her grandmother was a hyper-osmic, and she encouraged Joy as a child to make the most of her abilities, quizzing her on different varieties of rose,
sentences.zh: 她的祖母就是一个超常嗅觉者，并在乔伊小时候鼓励她充分发挥这一能力，通过让她辨别不同品种的玫瑰来对她进行测验，

sentences.en: teaching her to distinguish the scent of the petals from the scent of the leaves, from the scent of the pistils and stamens.
sentences.zh: 教导她区分花瓣的气味、叶子的气味，以及雌蕊和雄蕊的气味。

sentences.en: Still, her grandmother did not think odor of any kind to be a polite topic of conversation, and however rich and enjoyable and dense with information the olfactory world might be,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，她的祖母并不认为任何气味是得体的谈话话题，无论嗅觉世界多么丰富、美妙且充满信息，

sentences.en: she urged her granddaughter to keep her experience of it to herself.
sentences.zh: 她还是敦促孙女把自己的体验留在心里。

sentences.en: Les only learned of Joy's peculiar nose well after their relationship began on a trip to the Scandinavian far north.
sentences.zh: 莱斯直到他们的恋情开始很久之后，才在一次斯堪的纳维亚远北之旅中知道了乔伊那奇怪的鼻子。

sentences.en: Joy would not stop going on about the creamy odor of the tundra, or what she insisted was the aroma of the cold itself.
sentences.zh: 乔伊喋喋不休地谈论着苔原那种奶油般的气味，或者她坚称那是寒冷本身的气味。

sentences.en: Joy planned to go off to university in Paris or Rome.
sentences.zh: 乔伊原本打算去巴黎或罗马的大学深造。

sentences.en: Faced with the prospect of tending to his mother alone, however,
sentences.zh: 然而，面对独自照顾母亲的前景，

sentences.en: Les begged her to stay in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 莱斯恳求她留在苏格兰。

sentences.en: He trained as a doctor, she as a nurse.
sentences.zh: 他接受了医科培训，她则接受了护士培训。

sentences.en: They married during his residency.
sentences.zh: 他们在他的住院医师实习期间结了婚。

sentences.en: He was soon the sort of capable young physician one might hope to meet, a practitioner of uncommon enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 不久后，他便成了人们希望遇到的那种精干的年轻医生，一位充满罕见热情的全科医生。

sentences.en: And shortly after his 30th birthday, he was appointed consultant anesthesiologist at Macclesfield District General Hospital outside Manchester in England,
sentences.zh: 在他30岁生日后不久，他被任命为英格兰曼彻斯特郊外麦克尔斯菲尔德区综合医院的顾问麻醉师，

sentences.en: the first in his graduating class to make consultant.
sentences.zh: 成为他那一届毕业生中第一个升任顾问医生的人。

sentences.en: The Milnes installed themselves in an ancient stone farmhouse high on a country hill in Cheshire.
sentences.zh: 米尔恩一家搬进了柴郡乡村山丘高处的一座古老石头农舍里。

sentences.en: By then, they had three young sons, and the edifice, which was old enough to be listed in the Doomsday Book of 1086, was a happy, never-ending project.
sentences.zh: 那时，他们有三个年幼的儿子，这座古老到足以被收录进1086年《末日审判书》中的建筑，成了一个快乐且永无止境的修缮项目。

sentences.en: They threw elaborate boozy dinner parties.
sentences.zh: 他们举办了精致而充满美酒的晚宴。

sentences.en: They kept geese and hens and took in stray cats, dogs, a duck.
sentences.zh: 他们养了鹅和母鸡，还收养了流浪猫、狗和一只鸭子。

sentences.en: We just seemed to get on and do things,
sentences.zh: “我们似乎就是合得来，而且总能把事情做好，”

sentences.en: Joy told me.
sentences.zh: 乔伊对我说。

sentences.en: Friends still liken her to Mary Poppins, part twinkly magic, part no-frills practicality.
sentences.zh: 朋友们至今仍把她比作玛丽·波平斯，既带着闪烁的魔法，又有着不搞虚架子的务实。

sentences.en: She considers herself to be a never-stop person, she said.
sentences.zh: 她说，她认为自己是一个永不停歇的人。

sentences.en: Her husband was the same.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫也是如此。

sentences.en: Les spent long hours in the surgical theater, which in Macclesfield had little in the way of ventilation, and Joy typically found that he came home smelling of anesthetics,
sentences.zh: 莱斯在手术室里度过了漫长的时间，麦克尔斯菲尔德的手术室几乎没什么通风设施，乔伊通常发现他回家时身上带着麻醉剂的气味、

sentences.en: antiseptics, and blood.
sentences.zh: 消毒剂的气味和血腥味。

sentences.en: But he returned one August evening in 1982, shortly after his 32nd birthday, smelling of something new and distinctly unsavory, of some thick muSt.
sentences.zh: 但在1982年8月的一个傍晚，在他32岁生日刚过不久，他回家时却带着一种崭新且明显令人讨厌的气味，一股浓烈的霉味。

sentences.en: From then on, the odor never ceased, though neither Les nor almost anyone but his wife could detect it.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，这种气味就再也没有消失过，尽管莱斯本人以及除了他妻子之外的几乎所有人都闻不到。

sentences.en: For Joy, even a small shift in her husband's aroma might have been cause for distress, but his scent now seemed to have changed fundamentally,
sentences.zh: 对乔伊来说，丈夫气味的哪怕一点点改变都可能成为担忧的理由，但他的气味现在似乎从根本上发生了变化，

sentences.en: as if replaced by that of someone else.
sentences.zh: 仿佛被另一个人的气味所取代。

sentences.en: She thought he smelled vaguely of his mother.
sentences.zh: 她觉得他闻起来隐约有点像他的母亲。

sentences.en: Les had lately begun to change in other ways, however, and soon the smell came to seem almost trivial.
sentences.zh: 然而，莱斯最近在其他方面也开始发生变化，很快这种气味就显得几乎微不足道了。

sentences.en: It was as if his personality had shifted.
sentences.zh: 就好像他的性格变了。

sentences.en: Les had rather suddenly become detached, ill-tempered, apathetic.
sentences.zh: 莱斯相当突然地变得冷漠、脾气暴躁、无精打采。

sentences.en: He ceased helping out with many household chores.
sentences.zh: 他不再帮忙做许多家务。

sentences.en: He snapped at his boys.
sentences.zh: 他会对儿子们发脾气。

sentences.en: At parties out, he took to behaving in an excessive, theatrically buoyant way before returning home to collapse in exhaustion.
sentences.zh: 在出去参加派对时，他开始表现出一种过度的、充满戏剧性的亢奋行为，然后回到家累得瘫倒在地。

sentences.en: Joy felt these performances were meant in part to spite her, to prove that her complaints about his new demeanor were unfounded.
sentences.zh: 乔伊觉得这些表现部分是为了气她，证明她对他新表现的抱怨是毫无根据的。

sentences.en: There was no empathy, she says.
sentences.zh: 她说，他完全没有同理心。

sentences.en: An odd physical deterioration also seemed to have begun.
sentences.zh: 一种奇怪的身体退化似乎也已经开始。

sentences.en: At the house, he was awkward with the mower.
sentences.zh: 在家里，他用割草机时显得笨手笨脚。

sentences.en: On a vacation to the Scottish coast, he and his sons took sailing lessons.
sentences.zh: 在苏格兰海岸度假时，他和儿子们一起上了帆船课。

sentences.en: The boys took to it quickly, but Les could not work out the timing.
sentences.zh: 儿子们很快就学会了，但莱斯却掌握不好时机。

sentences.en: A golf club slipped from his hands mid-swing.
sentences.zh: 挥杆时，高尔夫球杆从他手中滑落。

sentences.en: Playing darts at a friend's house, he somehow managed to throw one into his foot.
sentences.zh: 在朋友家里玩飞镖时，他竟然把一支飞镖扔进了自己的脚里。

sentences.en: Les's sleep, too, was increasingly disturbed, and bizarrely, he began acting out his dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 莱斯的睡眠也越来越不安稳，诡异的是，他开始把梦境在现实中演绎出来。

sentences.en: He once dreamed of catching a burglar.
sentences.zh: 他曾梦见自己抓住了一个小偷。

sentences.en: Joy lied to friends and colleagues about the source of the bruises she was left with, thinking no one would believe that her husband had attacked her as he slept.
sentences.zh: 乔伊向朋友和同事谎称身上瘀伤的来源，她认为没有人会相信她的丈夫在睡梦中袭击了她。

sentences.en: Nor, at Les's unequivocal demand, did she speak a word of his newfound impotence.
sentences.zh: 而且，由于莱斯明确的要求，她对他的新发阳痿一字不说。

sentences.en: In private, he laid the blame on her.
sentences.zh: 私底下，他把责任归咎于她。

sentences.en: She had grown too fat, he said, to be of any possible intereSt.
sentences.zh: 他说她长得太胖了，已经引不起任何兴趣了。

sentences.en: The man Joy married had no such cruelty in him.
sentences.zh: 乔伊嫁的那个男人身上根本没有这种残酷。

sentences.en: She considered leaving.
sentences.zh: 她曾考虑过离开。

sentences.en: After more than a decade of alienation and resentment, however, it began to occur to her that the changes in her husband might have some organic cause, that they might be
sentences.zh: 然而，在经历了十多年的疏离和怨恨之后，她开始觉得丈夫身上的变化可能有着某种器质性原因，它们可能是

sentences.en: symptoms of some disease.
sentences.zh: 某种疾病的症状。

sentences.en: When he began referring to the other person, a shadow off to his side, she suspected a brain tumor.
sentences.zh: 当他开始提到另一个人——一个站在他身旁的阴影时，她怀疑是脑瘤。

sentences.en: Eventually, she prevailed upon him to see his doctor, who referred him to a neurologist in Manchester.
sentences.zh: 最终，她劝说他去看医生，后者将他转诊给了曼彻斯特的一位神经科医生。

sentences.en: Parkinson's disease is typically classed as a movement disorder, and its most familiar symptoms, tremor, rigidity, a slowing known as bradykinesia, are indeed motoric.
sentences.zh: 帕金森病通常被归类为运动障碍，其最熟悉的症状——震颤、僵硬、被称为运动迟缓的动作变慢——确实是运动方面的。

sentences.en: But the disease's autonomic, psychological, and cognitive symptoms are no less terrible and commonly begin during the so-called prodrome, years before any changes in movement.
sentences.zh: 但该病的自主神经、心理和认知症状同样可怕，并且通常在所谓的“前驱期”就开始出现，比任何运动方面的变化都要早几年。

sentences.en: And yet, they do not suggest a diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些症状并不会让人联想到确诊。

sentences.en: Irritability, fatigue, troubled sleep, these are extremely common among the well, and among the infirm, they can be associated with any number of conditions.
